comment: Shared cross-language fixture manifest. Every implementation of the web_fetch:v1 wire contract - the Rust contracts crate, the Python control-plane adapter, and any future Go rewrite - runs this same list and must agree on every verdict. 'valid' is the only assertion; 'reason' documents why the case exists.

requests.reason: URL alone; format defaults to markdown.
Inert HTML source is a supported format.
Plain HTTP and text output are supported.
Formats outside the enum are not silently coerced to the default.
The caller may not supply headers or credentials.
The caller may not supply images or commands.
There is no per-request inspection bypass.
The caller may not supply detection rules.
URL userinfo carries credentials to the destination.
Only http and https are fetched.

envelopes.reason: The design's worked success example.
A 4xx body that passed inspection is returned with its actual status.
Source text shaped like an envelope stays inert inside data.content.
The design's worked rejection example.
An incomplete scan withholds content.
A destination refusal never runs inspection, so policy_id is null.
A limit failure returns no scanned prefix.
Only a completed no_match inspection permits success.
An absent policy cannot produce success.
ok requires typed non-null data.
A rejection must carry no body.
Error messages are fixed; they cannot embed a URL or matched text.
Unsupported envelope versions are refused, not best-effort parsed.
Unknown envelope fields are refused, including ones that look like grants.
trust is a fixed enum; fetched data cannot claim to be internal.
Unknown payload fields are refused, including download handles.
final_url is validated like the request URL.
conversion_method is a fixed server-owned enum; no remote reader exists.
Every failure carries a code.
Codes come from the fixed table; no code invites a weaker retry.
v1 processes a documented set of text media types; nothing else can be carried in a result.
